description: Sync knowledge articles, catalog items, ticket rows and custom-table rows from the ServiceNow resources you choose. ServiceNow read access carries over where its rules can be read and Enforce ACL is on.
opening: Sync the ServiceNow knowledge bases, service catalogs, ticket tables and custom tables you select. Each knowledge article, catalog item and table row is one document. Comments and work notes are searchable with the record they belong to, and attachments are read when the service account can download them and their format is supported.

Readers come from knowledge-base and catalog-item criteria and from table read rules. Rules with conditions or scripts cannot be captured, and standard ticket tables often use them. Search applies captured readers only when Enforce ACL is on. Work notes share their record's readers. Rows deleted in ServiceNow can stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: A knowledge article can be read by the users its knowledge base's Can Read criteria allow, minus those its Cannot Read criteria exclude. A knowledge base with no criteria follows the instance's policy for that case. When the instance turns on article-level criteria, an article is limited further to users both allow. A catalog item can be read by the users its own criteria allow. Catalogs themselves carry no readers. A ticket or custom-table row can be read by users who hold the roles its table's read rules require, across the table and its parent tables, including roles held through a group. Comments and work notes share their record's readers. Rules that resolve to no users leave the item readable by no one.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a read rule has a condition or script, uses advanced user criteria, or yields more users than HydraDB can capture, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: Standard ticket-table read rules often use scripts, so on many instances ticket readers cannot be captured. Set an access rule on such tables.
If an article's own criteria cannot be read, the article follows its knowledge base's readers, with a warning. That can be wider than the article's own rule.
Work notes are marked internal in ServiceNow, but they have no separate readers in HydraDB.

connect.auth: ServiceNow uses an OAuth application with the client credentials grant. Its OAuth Application User is a dedicated service account. Basic authentication is not supported, and HydraDB never stores a user password.

credentials.name: instance
credentials.text: The instance name only, for example `acme` for `acme.service-now.com`.

credentials.name: client_id
credentials.text: The client id of the OAuth application.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: The client secret of that application.

permissions.name: admin
permissions.text: required. Reads every selected table, the lists HydraDB offers for selection, comments, work notes and attachments.

permissions.name: snc_read_only
permissions.text: required. Blocks every write from the service account, so it can only read.

connect.permissions_note: Reading permissions needs `admin` and `snc_read_only`, or read access to `sys_security_acl`, `sys_security_acl_role`, `user_criteria`, `sys_user`, `sys_user_has_role`, `sys_group_has_role` and `sys_user_grmember`.

steps.title: Create a service account
steps.text: In ServiceNow, create a dedicated web-service user and give it the `admin` and `snc_read_only` roles. Set its timezone to GMT, so date windows line up as expected.

steps.title: Create an OAuth application
steps.text: Create an OAuth application for the client credentials grant, and set the service user as its OAuth Application User.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Enter the instance name, not the URL, as `instance`, then the client id and client secret.

steps.title: Select resources
steps.text: HydraDB lists the instance's knowledge bases, service catalogs, ticket tables and custom tables. Select the ones to sync. Nothing outside your selection is read. Each ticket table reads only rows of its exact class, so selecting a parent table does not bring in its child tables' rows, and selecting both never indexes a row twice.

connect.account: One connector reads one ServiceNow instance.

sync.first_sync: Each selected resource reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Only published, latest-version articles and active catalog items are read.
sync.changes: Each selected resource syncs on its own and reads rows updated since the last sync. A record whose comment, work note or attachment changed is read again too.
sync.edits: An updated row is read again and updates its document. A new version of an article updates the same document, keyed by the article number.
sync.deletes: Rows deleted in ServiceNow can stay searchable in HydraDB. An article that is retired, or a catalog item that is deactivated, is not removed when it stops being read.
notes: A service account without access to comments and work notes can get an empty answer instead of an error, so a ticket can sync without them.
A catalog item in several selected catalogs is one document, filed under the selected catalog with the lowest id.

shared_attributes.name: comments
shared_attributes.text: Comments and work notes the service account can read, each with its author and time, searchable with the record. The graph records each author.

shared_attributes.name: attachments
shared_attributes.text: Text read from attached files that downloaded and parsed successfully, searchable with the record. Each keeps a link to the original file.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.servicenow_table
shared_attributes.text: The source table, such as `incident` or `kb_knowledge`. Limits a query to one table. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.servicenow_kind
shared_attributes.text: Whether the item is an article, catalog item, ticket or custom row. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.servicenow_sys_id
shared_attributes.text: The row's current sys_id. Targets one row. For articles, use the number instead, because a new version has a new sys_id. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.sys_class_name
shared_attributes.text: The row's ServiceNow class, when supplied. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
shared_attributes.text: The selected knowledge base, catalog or table. Limits a query to it. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
shared_attributes.text: The name of the selected knowledge base, catalog or table, when available. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
shared_attributes.text: Whether the item came from a knowledge base, a catalog or a table. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: acl
shared_attributes.text: The users who can read the item, worked out as described under Permissions. Not searchable.

documents.name: Knowledge articles
documents.one_document: One knowledge article, in its published latest version.
documents.title: The short description, else the article number. Otherwise `ServiceNow article` and its id.
documents.text: The article text converted from HTML, else its wiki text, else the short description. The author and an `Updated` line are part of the text too. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the article was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The article in the ServiceNow knowledge view, by its number.
documents.files: Attachments the service account can download are read when their format is supported, up to 25 MiB by default. Image fields are not read. Not every file yields text.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The article's author. The graph records the article as written by that person.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_email
attributes.text: The author's email. Limits a query to one author, and identifies the author in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.number
attributes.text: The article number. Keeps every version of the article on one document, builds the link back, and becomes the title when there is no short description. Targets one article.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the article was last updated, written as an `Updated` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the article was created. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.workflow_state
attributes.text: The article's workflow state. Only published articles are synced. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.article_version
attributes.text: The article's version, when supplied. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.kb_category
attributes.text: The knowledge category. Limits a query to one category. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.language
attributes.text: The article's language code. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.text: The user name of the last editor. The editor is not attached to the article as a person.

attributes.name: published_at
attributes.text: When the article was published. It is not the result date.

documents.name: Catalog items
documents.title: The item name, else the short description. Otherwise `ServiceNow catalog item` and its id.
documents.text: The short description, then the full description converted from HTML. An `Updated` line is part of the text too. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the item was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.files: Attachments the service account can download are read when their format is supported, up to 25 MiB by default. Image fields are not read. Not every file yields text.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the item was last updated, written as an `Updated` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the item was created. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.number
attributes.text: The item's number, when it has one. Targets one item. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.category
attributes.text: The item's category. Limits a query to one category. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.text: The user name of the last editor.

documents.name: Tickets
documents.one_document: One row of a selected ticket table, such as an incident, problem, change request, request, requested item or catalog task, with its comments and work notes.
documents.title: The short description, else the ticket number. Otherwise `ServiceNow`, the table name and the row id.
documents.text: The description, then labeled sections when present: `Close notes`, `Resolution notes`, `Cause notes`, `Fix notes`, `Workaround`, `Implementation plan`, `Backout plan`, `Test plan` and `Justification`. The status, priority, assignee, reporter, ticket type, resolution date, parent and creation time are part of the text too, with the ticket's key. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the row was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.files: Attachments the service account can download are read when their format is supported, up to 25 MiB by default. Image fields are not read. Not every file yields text.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The displayed state.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: The displayed priority.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned person's name. The graph records the ticket as assigned to that person.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.assignee_email
attributes.text: The assignee's email. Limits a query to one assignee, and identifies the assignee in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: reporter
attributes.text: The caller, requested-for person or opener. The graph records the ticket as reported by that person.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.reporter_email
attributes.text: The reporter's email. Limits a query to one reporter, and identifies the reporter in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: ticket_type
attributes.text: The table's label, such as Incident.

attributes.name: resolved_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was resolved. It is not the result date.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The ticket's parent, else its requested item, else its request. Places the ticket under that record when its table is selected.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.number
attributes.text: The ticket number. Targets one ticket. Becomes the title when there is no short description.

attributes.name: external_id
attributes.text: The row's id, written into the text as the ticket's key. Keeps later syncs on the same document.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the row was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the row was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.assignment_group
attributes.text: The assignment group's name. Limits a query to one group. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.state_code
attributes.text: The raw state code. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.priority_code
attributes.text: The raw priority code. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.impact_code
attributes.text: The raw impact code. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.urgency_code
attributes.text: The raw urgency code. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.category
attributes.text: The ticket's category. Not searchable.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.text: The ticket's deadline.

attributes.name: custom_fields
attributes.text: Impact, urgency, severity, subcategory, close and resolution codes, contact type, approval, risk, referenced names, and opened and closed dates.

documents.name: Custom table rows
documents.one_document: One row of a selected custom table.
documents.title: The table's display field, else `name`, `u_name`, the number or the short description. Otherwise `ServiceNow`, the table name and the row id.
documents.text: The row's non-empty text columns as `Label: value` lines, converted from HTML. The title is used when there are none.
documents.date: When the row was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.files: Attachments the service account can download are read when their format is supported, up to 25 MiB by default. Image fields are not read. Not every file yields text.

attributes.name: Text columns
attributes.text: The row's non-empty text columns, with their display labels.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the row was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the row was created. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.number
attributes.text: The row's number, when it has one. Targets one row. Not searchable.

attributes.name: table
attributes.text: The custom table's name. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.servicenow_table`.

example_searches: How was the VPN outage incident resolved?
What does the knowledge base say about requesting a new laptop?
What work notes were left on change CHG0030012?

connections: A ticket to its parent, else its requested item, else its request, and to any other of the three.
A ticket to its problem and to the record that caused it.
A ticket to its change request.
A link reaches a record only when that record's table is selected.
Each item is grouped under the knowledge base, catalog or table it came from.
people: The assignee and reporter of each ticket.
The author of each comment and work note.
The assignment group is a filter, not a person or group in the graph.
graph.from_text: Descriptions, resolution and plan notes, comments and work notes, article text, and text read from attachments.

not_synced: Knowledge bases, catalogs and tables you did not select.
Unpublished and older article versions, and inactive catalog items.
Users, groups, CMDB items, journal entries and attachments as documents of their own.
Image fields, files over the download limit, and files whose text cannot be read.
Comments, work notes and attachments the service account cannot read.
